t:
Section 14 of such Act is amended to read as follows:


“learners, apprentices, students, and handicapped workers
“Sec. 14. (a) The Secretary of Labor, to the extent necessary in order to prevent curtailment of opportunities for employment, shall by regulations or by orders provide for the employment of learners, of apprentices, and of messengers employed primarily in delivering letters and messages, under special certificates issued pursuant to regulations of the Secretary, at such wages lower than the minimum wage applicable under section 6 and subject to such limitations as to time, number, proportion, and length of service as the Secretary shall prescribe.
“(b) The Secretary, to the extent necessary in order to prevent curtailment of opportunities for employment, shall by regulation or order provide for the employment or full-time students, regardless of age but in compliance with applicable child labor laws, on a part-time basis in retail or service establishments (not to exceed twenty hours in any workweek) or on a part-time or a full-time basis in such establishments during school vacations, under special certificates issued pursuant to regulations of the Secretary, at a wage rate not less than 85 per centum of the minimum wage applicable under section 6, except that the proportion of student hours of employment to total hours of employment of all employees in any establishment may not exceed (1) such proportion for the corresponding month of the twelve month period preceding May 1, 1961, (2) in the case of a retail or service establishment whose employees (other than employees engaged in commerce or in the production of goods for commerce) are covered by this Act for the first time on or after the effective date of the Fair Labor Standards Amendments of 1966, such proportion for the corresponding month of the twelve month period immediately prior to such date, or (3) in the case of a retail or service establishment coming into existence after May 1, 1961, or a retail or service establishment for which records of student hours worked are not available, a proportion of student hours of employment to total hours of employment of all employees based on the practice during the twelve-month period preceding May 1, 1961, in (A) similar establishments of the same employer in the same general metropolitan area in which the new establishment is located, (B) similar establishments of the same employer in the same or nearby counties if the new establishment is not in a metropolitan area, or (C) other establishments of the same general character operating in the community or the nearest comparable community. Before the Secretary may issue a certificate under this subsection he must find that such employment will not create a substantial probability of reducing the full-time employment opportunities of persons other than those employed under this subsection.

“(c) 
The Secretary, to the extent necessary in order to prevent curtailment of opportunities for employment, shall by certificate or order provide for the employment of full-time students, regardless of age but in compliance with applicable child labor laws, on a part-time basis in agriculture (not to exceed twenty hours in any workweek) or on a part-time or a full-time basis in agriculture during school vacations, at a wage rate not less than 85 per centum of the minimum wage applicable under section 6. Before the Secretary may issue a certificate or order under this subsection he must find that such employment will not create a substantial probability of reducing the full-time employment opportunities of persons other than those employed under this subsection.
“(d) (1) Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2) and (3) of this subsection, the Secretary of Labor, to the extent necessary in order to prevent curtailment of opportunities for employment, shall by regulation or order provide for the employment under special certificates of individuals (including individuals employed in agriculture) whose earning or productive capacity is impaired by age or physical or mental deficiency or injury, at wages which are lower than the minimum wage applicable under section 6 of this Act but not less than 50 per centum of such wage and which are commensurate with those paid nonhandicapped workers in industry in the vicinity for essentially the same type, quality, and quantity of work.

“(2) 
The Secretary, pursuant to such regulations as he shall prescribe and upon certification of the State agency administering or supervising the administration of vocational rehabilitation services, may issue special certificates for the employment of—

“(A) 
handicapped workers engaged in work which is incidental to training or evaluation programs, and


“(B) 
multi-handicapped individuals and other individuals whose earning capacity is so severely impaired that they are unable to engage in competitive employment,
at wages which are less than those required by this subsection and which are related to the worker’s productivity.
“(3) (A) The Secretary may by regulation or order provide for the employment of handicapped clients in work activities centers under special certificates at wages which are less than the minimums applicable under section 6 of this Act or prescribed by paragraph (1) of this subsection and which constitute equitable compensation for such clients in work activities centers.

“(B) For purposes of this section, the term ‘work activities centers’ shall mean centers planned and designed exclusively to provide therapeutic activities for handicapped clients whose physical or mental impairment is so severe as to make their productive capacity inconsequential.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a licensing scheme in which employers apply for special sub-minimum-wage certificates, and applications are not participation. But the section repeatedly directs the Secretary of Labor to act "by regulations or by orders", and a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation under the definition. It also conditions certain federal certificates on certification by a State vocational rehabilitation agency, which brings a non-federal government into the federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of Labor to issue regulations and special certificates for employment. While it mentions certification by a State agency for handicapped workers, this is part of the administrative process for issuing a specific certificate (similar to a license or benefit application), which the definition excludes. There is no requirement for public comment, public hearings, or consultation with outside entities regarding the creation of the regulations themselves.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Labor, to the extent necessary in order to prevent curtailment of opportunities for employment, shall by regulations or by orders provide for the employment of learners, of apprentices, and of messengers employed primarily in delivering letters and messages, under special certificates issued pursuant to regulations of the Secretary
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the Secretary to consult with or receive certification from a "State agency" (subsection d(2)) constitutes participation because states are outside the federal government. However, this certification is part of the administrative process for issuing a specific employment certificate to an individual or entity, which functions more like a licensing or benefit application process rather than a broad consultation on a federal policy decision. Furthermore, the primary mechanism described is the Secretary issuing regulations and orders unilaterally, based on findings, without a mandated public comment period, advisory board with outside members, or consultation with the general public or other outside entities before making the regulatory decision itself. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or licenses. The state agency certification is a prerequisite for the certificate issuance, akin to a verification step in an application process, not a participatory decision-making role for the state in the formulation of the federal rule.

opus.w: The section repeatedly directs the Secretary of Labor to act 'by regulations,' and the definition counts required or authorized rulemaking as participation. Subsection (d)(2) also makes a state agency's certification a condition for the Secretary's federal decision, which brings a party outside the federal government into that decision. Reading the certificates as mere license applications misses both the rulemaking requirement and the role of the state agency.
opus.s: The Secretary, pursuant to such regulations as he shall prescribe and upon certification of the State agency administering or supervising the administration of vocational rehabilitation services, may issue special certificates
opus.b:
1. **Tempting wrong reading:** The section is mostly about special certificates that employers obtain to pay below minimum wage. Those look like license applications, which the definition excludes. But the section also tells the Secretary of Labor to act "by regulations." Under the definition and Example 6, requiring or authorizing rulemaking counts as participation, because rulemaking brings in public notice and comment. Separately, under (d)(2) the Secretary can issue certain certificates only after a state agency certifies them. A state agency is outside the federal government.

2. **Label:** Yes.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the process for issuing special employment certificates (a form of license or benefit) to specific groups of workers. While it mentions certification by a State agency, this is an administrative condition for issuing the certificate, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a broader policy decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, or licenses. There is no mention of public comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or required consultation with outside entities regarding the creation of the regulations themselves.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the Secretary to find that employment "will not create a substantial probability of reducing the full-time employment opportunities" implies a consultation with affected workers or unions. However, the text does not mandate any such consultation; it only mandates an internal finding by the Secretary. The references to "certification of the State agency" are administrative prerequisites for issuing a certificate (a benefit/license), not a participatory process in a federal policy decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants.
